messages:
maria (Support): Hey team — AcmeSupport forwarded an escalation: sudden p95/p99 spikes on POST /v1/tool-call after they added tool output JSON schemas. They see p95 jump ~200ms -> 1.1s and p99 up to ~1.8s. Happening in multiple regions. They included a small reproducible curl and one x-request-id.

jordan (Customer Success): x-request-id=02GJH8N4B1LQY0C2 (2026-03-12 14:03 UTC). Customer repro'd against hosted API. Said removing schema block returns latency to normal.

maria (Support): grabbing traces/logs now. Short trace summary below.

--- TRACE SUMMARY ---
spans: gateway -> auth -> router -> tool-router -> runtime
router p95 baseline ~110ms -> observed 600-1.2s in window
tool-router p95 200ms -> ~950ms; p99 ~1.6-1.9s
--- END TRACE ---

log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:03:12Z] x-request-id=02GJH8N4B1LQY0C2 VALIDATION START schema_id=acme.invoice.v2
[2026-03-12T14:03:12Z] x-request-id=02GJH8N4B1LQY0C2 VALIDATION STEP nodes=312 duration_ms=510
[2026-03-12T14:03:12Z] x-request-id=02GJH8N4B1LQY0C2 TOOL-ROUTER DISPATCH dispatch_ms=28
[2026-03-12T14:03:12Z] x-request-id=02GJH8N4B1LQY0C2 RUNTIME CALL model=redwood-quant-1 seq=96 runtime_ms=150
```

maria (Support): Customer repro (sanitized):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"create invoice","tools":[{"name":"format_invoice","schema":{...large schema...}}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool-call
```

ankit (Eng Runtime): quick diagnosis: router currently runs full JSON Schema validation sync using our Node validator compiled per-request in many code paths. Complex schemas (200-400 nodes) take ~300-600ms if not compiled/cached — matches logs. Tool-router is single-threaded per worker so this stacks on request latency.

ankit (Eng Runtime): baseline metrics (us-west-2 24h): no-schema p95 ~180ms p99 ~420ms; schema-present p95 ~650-1200ms, p99 to ~1.8s. Schema-using requests are ~3-6% overall but concentrated traffic from a few customers causing SLO noise.

lina (Eng Platform): added note — tool-router also does live metadata enrichment via tool-discovery HTTP call (20-60ms tail). Discovery has short cache TTL; combined with sync validation it aggregates tail time. No compiled-validator artifact cached today.

kevin (SRE): mitigation brainstorm (fast to medium):
- immediate fast: offer customer opt-out header `X-RW-Skip-Tool-Validation: 1` behind enterprise feature flag. Cuts ~400-600ms in their case.
- fast2: route that customer's workspace to a higher-concurrency router pool to reduce queuing/tails.
- medium: implement compiled-validator LRU cache keyed by schema hash; cheap and effective.
- medium/long: switch to faster validator (wasm or Rust binding) or async post-validation.

maria (Support): I tested the opt-out header with Acme in a staging workspace; they reported p95 back to ~210ms and p99 ~430ms. They are understandably cautious about turning off server-side schema enforcement.

ankit (Eng Runtime): proposal for safe rollout:
1) short-term: enable per-customer opt-out if approved. Add guard so free/public accounts cannot use it.
2) immediate dev work: implement per-worker compiled-validator cache (LRU, size tuned) — should reduce validation to ~50-80ms for repeated schemas.
3) medium: prototype wasm-based validator for the router (benchmarks show 3-5x speedup in our tests).
4) long: provide async full validation + alerting/telemetry when validation fails, allowing fast request path to proceed but detect invalid outputs.

lina (Eng Platform): platform tasks: extend tool metadata cache to store compiled validator artifacts; add per-customer routing config to move traffic to dedicated pools. (Owners: lina, ETA: metadata cache + routing rule in ~3 working days)

kevin (SRE): monitoring changes to add: schema_validation_time_ms p50/p95/p99 tagged by customer_id and schema_hash; add a synthetic that hits tool-call with a large schema every 15m to detect regressions. (owner kevin)

maria (Support): Repro steps for eng: simulate sustained customer load with large schema:
1) use hey/vegeta to send repeated requests with the schema payload at 40-60 RPS for 60s.
2) capture x-request-id and watch router logs for VALIDATION slow events.
Example:
```
hey -n 3600 -c 50 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -m POST -T application/json -d '{"input":"gen","tools":[{"name":"format","schema":<big_schema>}]} ' https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/tool-call
```

ankit (Eng Runtime): local benchmark results: compiled+cached validator avg ~55ms; compiled-on-each-request ~420ms; wasm prototype ~15-20ms. So caching is an immediate high ROI change.

lina (Eng Platform): policy: opt-out must be explicit and documented; only enterprise workspaces can request it. We'll add a short-term rollout guard and audit logs when it's used.

maria (Support): message to customer drafted: "Weve identified server-side JSON schema validation as the primary source of tail latency. We can enable a temporary validation opt-out for your workspace to reduce latency immediately while we deploy permanent performance fixes (validator caching + wasm). This will disable server-side enforcement of tool output shapes; we can offer to run a sample validation on a copy of your traffic before enabling the opt-out. Reply with approval to proceed." 

jordan (Customer Success): Acme approved opt-out. I flipped the flag at 15:12 UTC. Observed post-flip: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~450ms in their workspace; no uptick in validation-related errors for 50m of monitoring.

ankit (Eng Runtime): dev action items (flat list):
- add LRU compiled-validator cache in tool-router (ankit, PR forthcoming, ETA 4d)
- prototype wasm validator (ankit + research, ETA 2w)
- design async post-validation & telemetry (ankit, ETA 3w)

lina (Eng Platform): infra action items:
- add dedicated router pool + routing rule for opt-outs (lina, ETA 2d)
- increase discovery cache TTL and attach metadata-cache for compiled artifacts (lina, ETA 5d)

kevin (SRE): monitoring/action: canary deployment of compiled-validator cache to 5%; expected p95 validation time reduction ~70% on canary hosts. Add alert rule if error rate increases by 0.5% above baseline.

deploy-bot: CI passed for compiled-validator PR in staging; canary rollout started to 5%.

kevin (SRE): first-canary metrics (1h): validation p95 down ~68% on canary, no error increase observed.

maria (Support): closing the loop with Acme: theyre satisfied with the temporary opt-out. They asked for ETA for permanent fix; I linked them to the dev timeline and will follow up when compiled-cache lands.

ankit (Eng Runtime): notes for postmortem: root cause = synchronous deep JSON schema validation (no compiled cache) in tool-router + extra discovery lookup tail; mitigation: customer opt-out, compiled-validator cache PR, discovery TTL bump, routing rule, monitoring added.

maria (Support): marking ticket as escalated -> eng-runtime. Leaving thread pinned for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
